industries.narrative: Full breadth (5/5 up) with a solid cap-weighted +0.96%, but relative volume is soft (0.25x) — clean tape, not conviction-driven.

sector_breadth_notes.note: Sector strength is narrow: Auto Manufacturers lead cleanly while Auto & Truck Dealerships (2.96) and Personal Services (2.75) drag — this is an OEM/EV-driven move, not broad consumer cyclical.
Insurance is a clear drag (Life 2.62, P&C 3.02); sector strength must be coming from banks/capital markets, not shown in the qualifying list.
Communication Services looks internally weak — Internet Content (2.69) and Ad Agencies (2.81) both laggards; sector ETF strength is likely mega-cap concentrated, not broad.
Trucking (2.60) and Security Services (3.05) laggards suggest goods-movement weakness; industrial strength is not cyclical/transport driven.
Regulated Water (2.70) and Renewables (2.93) both weak — utility strength is defensive/regulated electric, not the growth-linked subgroups.

key_divergences: Only 1 industry cleared the 6.5 gate across 6 qualifying sectors — sector-level strength is being driven by mega-caps and narrow subgroups, not broad industry participation. Insurance dragging XLF and Internet Content dragging XLC are the sharpest internal contradictions.
leadership_theme: Autos/EVs lead alone; sector moves are narrow and mega-cap driven, not broad-based
